high.title: Interest Rates Rise Sharply: How Much Are Households and Businesses Depositing into the Banking System?
high.summary: As of June 26, 2026, total capital mobilization by credit institutions grew 5.02% year-to-date (vs. 6.11% at the same point in 2025), while credit growth reached 7.41% (vs. 8.3% a year prior), according to the Ministry of Finance's Statistics Department. Based on the SBV's end-2025 total deposit base of VND 16.5 quadrillion, this implies approximately VND 830 trillion (~USD 32.5bn) in net new deposits were added in H1 2026. The driver is clear: deposit rates have risen significantly, with the publicly quoted 12-month rate now at 7.0–7.5% p.a., while numerous banks are offering 8.5–9.0% p.a. on 6–12 month tenors for qualifying customers (new clients, VIP clients, or large deposits).

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of July 6: ACB Leads at 7.3%/year for 12-Month Terms Across Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank
high.summary: A survey of online deposit rate schedules as of July 6 shows Vietnamese banks maintaining the interest rate policies established in late June, with no broad-based upward or downward shift. The market leader on rates is ACB at 7.3%/year for 12-month deposits, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2%/year. A cluster of six banks — MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, VIB, and others — are offering 7.0%/year for 12-month terms, while LPBank, BVBank, Bac A Bank, and OCB are grouped at 6.9%/year. State-owned banks (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) continue to anchor the lower end of the deposit rate spectrum.

high.title: Banks' Outlook on Profit Growth, Credit Growth, and Capital Mobilization Going Forward
high.summary:
Based on a survey of Vietnamese credit institutions (CIs), the banking sector's overall business conditions and pre-tax profits in Q2/2026 continued to improve quarter-on-quarter, though falling short of previous survey expectations. Looking ahead, **84.1% of CIs expect positive pre-tax profit growth in full-year 2026** vs. 2025, while 10.6% fear negative growth and 5.3% expect no change. Critically for macro watchers, **credit growth expectations for 2026 have been revised down to 14.5%** (a 1.5 percentage point reduction from the prior survey), while **deposit/funding growth expectations were also trimmed to 14.3%** (down 1.6pp). For Q3/2026, CIs expect both deposit mobilization and credit outstanding to grow at an average of 4.2%. The downward revision in credit and deposit growth forecasts is a key signal for VND liquidity conditions — softer credit demand could ease upward pressure on lending rates but may also reflect cautious economic sentiment. Bond investors should note that moderating credit growth reduces competitive pressure on government bond yields from the banking sector's funding side. Watch for SBV's formal credit growth target reaffirmation later in Q3.

---

high.title: Three Scenarios for Vietnamese Stock Market in July 2026
high.summary:
In its July strategy report, Tien Phong Securities (TPS) outlines an improved macro backdrop for Vietnamese markets. Key positive drivers cited include: easing Middle East geopolitical risks reducing energy price pressures, USD/VND exchange rate stability, and signs of interest rate stress abating. The government's continued commitment to pro-growth policies, alongside positive Q2 GDP momentum and expected strong Q2 corporate earnings, are seen as consolidating investor confidence heading into July.

Critically for FX and fixed income traders, TPS notes that USD/VND stability — while not directly a catalyst for equity upside — serves as a foundational condition for a favorable investment environment. The report implies that when exchange rate risk subsides, foreign and domestic capital allocation toward equities becomes more comfortable. Three market scenarios are presented (detail truncated in source), framed around whether macro stability holds. **Key watch:** any deterioration in VND stability could rapidly shift TPS's base case. This report signals that the market consensus is currently pricing in a benign FX and rates environment for July — a risk if USD strengthens globally.

---

medium.title: MASVN Expert: VN-Index in Accumulation Uptrend, 2 Key Sectors Expected to "Attract Money"
medium.summary:
Mr. Tran Quoc Toan, Branch Director at Mirae Asset Securities (MASVN), offers a constructive but cautious outlook for the VN-Index in H2 2026, characterizing the market as being in a "gradual accumulation uptrend" rather than a sharp rally. He expects intermittent volatility and consolidation phases, but maintains that the long-term structure remains bullish. Key macro catalysts cited include: (1) improving core corporate earnings, particularly as credit growth is expected to more meaningfully filter through to the real economy in H2; (2) liquidity support measures and capital adequacy improvements within the banking system; and (3) continued FDI inflows and public investment disbursement acting as economic growth pillars. Notably, the analyst flags that **a gradual decline in interest rates would be a significant positive catalyst** for equities. On the risk side, **sustained net foreign selling** is highlighted as the primary headwind to watch. For fund managers, the key takeaway is that if SBV maintains an accommodative rate stance and foreign outflows stabilize, the equity market has room to grind higher — making rate trajectory and foreign flow data the critical variables to monitor.

---

medium.title: From July 1, Banks Must Provide Account Balances and Suspicious Transactions to Tax Authorities
medium.summary: Effective July 1, 2026, Decree 252 (implementing the 2025 Tax Administration Law) mandates that credit institutions, foreign bank branches, payment service providers, and international card organizations must share taxpayer payment account information — including account holder names, account numbers linked to tax codes, branch locations, and opening/closing dates — with tax authorities on a monthly basis (due by the 10th of the following month). Banks must also report transaction-level data including volumes, values, transfer descriptions, and sender/receiver information for both domestic and cross-border transfers, flagging any abnormal transactions for tax compliance review.

medium.title: Fastest Capital-Raising Banks Over the Past 10 Years: One Bank Grew Nearly 10x, Vietcombank Now Leads the Pack
medium.summary: Over the decade from 2015 to 2025, the aggregate charter capital of 27 Vietnamese commercial banks surged from VND 260,600 billion to nearly VND 922,000 billion — a 3.5x increase, adding over VND 661,000 billion in capitalization. VPBank led in percentage growth terms among private banks, with at least one institution growing its capital base nearly tenfold. Vietcombank has emerged as the absolute leader in total charter capital among all banks. Capital was raised through a mix of stock dividends, private placements, rights offerings, and ESOP issuances. This trend reflects banks' drive to meet Basel II/III capital adequacy standards, expand credit capacity, and fund digital transformation.

medium.title: Vietnam's Aquatic Exports to China Surpass Half a Billion USD — Trade Flow Implications
medium.summary:
Vietnam's seafood exports to China and Hong Kong reached approximately **USD 1.5 billion in H1 2026**, representing a **37.9% year-on-year increase** and accounting for 25.8% of total Vietnamese seafood export turnover — the highest growth rate among all key export markets, according to VASEP (Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Processors). The standout product is lobster, with China spending over **USD 506 million** on Vietnamese lobster imports in just the first five months of 2026, a 44.3% YoY surge, making China the single largest consumer market for this commodity. Other strong contributors include shrimp, pangasius, mollusks, and live/frozen seafood. While this is a sector-specific trade story rather than a direct FX or monetary policy event, the broader implication is **positive for Vietnam's trade balance and current account**, which in turn supports VND stability. Strong export momentum into China — Vietnam's largest trading partner — contributes to USD inflows and reduces pressure on the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) to defend the dong. Fund managers should monitor whether this export strength sustains into H2 2026, as it could provide a buffer against any external FX headwinds.

---

medium.title: Dragon Capital Identifies a Market Paradox and Names Two Undervalued Stocks
medium.summary: Dragon Capital's senior equities director highlights that approximately **70% of VN-Index constituents (274 out of 396 stocks) have declined** since end-2025, with only 117 stocks posting gains — reflecting broad-based market correction pressure in H1/2026. Key headwinds cited include interest rate changes, US-Iran tensions, and general macro uncertainty weighing on investor sentiment. Despite near-term underperformance, Dragon Capital's DCDS fund maintained cumulative returns exceeding **70% over three years** (~19.4% p.a.), outperforming VN-Index's 18.4%. The breadth of the market decline (70% of stocks down) is a meaningful data point for international fund managers assessing Vietnam equity exposure — it suggests index-level resilience may be masking significant underlying weakness. The identification of undervalued names by a major institutional player like Dragon Capital could be an early signal of selective bottom-fishing in the market.

medium.title: A Major Bank Accelerates Dividend Payouts and Share Offering
medium.summary:
Military Commercial Joint Stock Bank (MB Bank, ticker: MBB) has announced a Board of Directors resolution to increase its charter capital through two sequential actions: first, issuing shares as stock dividends to existing shareholders, and then conducting a rights offering to existing shareholders via a public share sale. The bank plans to issue approximately 805.5 million new shares under the rights offering, targeting proceeds of nearly VND 8,055 billion (~USD 315 million). The capital raised will be deployed as follows: VND 3,170 billion for working capital loans to businesses, VND 4,180 billion for project financing and fixed asset loans, and approximately VND 705 billion for retail/consumer lending. For bond and equity investors, this capital raise is relevant as it signals MB Bank's intent to expand its loan book aggressively and strengthens its capital adequacy buffer. Watch for potential share dilution pressure on MBB equity in the near term, and monitor whether the rights offering is fully subscribed as an indicator of institutional appetite for Vietnamese banking sector exposure.

---

medium.title: New Regulations on Bank Account Balance and Transaction Data Sharing — All Account Holders Should Note
medium.summary: Effective July 1, 2026, Vietnamese credit institutions and payment intermediaries entered a new phase of mandatory user data sharing under Decree 252 (implementing the 2025 Tax Administration Law). All domestic banks, foreign bank branches, e-wallets, payment intermediaries, and cross-border payment service providers are now required to periodically report detailed customer account balances, transaction histories, and flagged abnormal cash flows to tax authorities. Previously, banks were only obligated to provide basic identifying information. This regulatory shift significantly expands the data perimeter that financial institutions must proactively surrender to regulators. For foreign investors, this signals increasing financial surveillance and formalization of Vietnam's banking data infrastructure — a structural development relevant to assessing AML/compliance risk and the operating environment for banking sector equities.

medium.title: Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, VPBank, Techcombank, ACB, and HDBank Make Forbes Global 2000 List
medium.summary: Eight Vietnamese banks were included in the Forbes Global 2000 (2026 edition), representing 8 of Vietnam's 9 total entries on the list. Vietcombank ranked highest at #890 globally with revenues of $5.21B, net profit of $1.37B, total assets of $96.84B, and market cap of $19.25B. BIDV ranked #967 and leads on total assets at $128.62B. This recognition underscores the dominant role of the banking sector in Vietnam's capital markets and economy. For equity investors, this provides international visibility and benchmarking context for the major state-owned and private banks that form the backbone of the VN-Index.

medium.title: PNJ Loses Its Billion-Dollar Market Cap Status on the Stock Exchange
medium.summary: Shares of PNJ (Phu Nhuan Jewelry), one of Vietnam's largest listed consumer companies, fell to the floor price for three consecutive sessions through July 7, 2026, wiping out nearly 20% of market value and erasing over VND 6,300 billion (~USD 247 million) in market capitalisation. The company has now dropped below the USD 1 billion market cap threshold. The selloff was triggered by news that the former Director of P-Lab — a wholly owned subsidiary of PNJ — was arrested and prosecuted in connection with an alleged cross-border diamond smuggling case involving over 28,000 diamonds. PNJ has issued a statement asserting that legal liability rests with the individual, not the company. **Market relevance:** While PNJ is a consumer/retail name rather than a financial stock, the scale of the drawdown (~USD 247M in 3 sessions) contributes to broader VN-Index weakness and foreign investor sentiment. International funds with Vietnam equity mandates should monitor any contagion effect on market confidence and assess whether forced selling by domestic funds creates wider market dislocation.
